chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Armstrong did not excite him; only Hodges and Carter did
summary: Holmes says he was only interested in saxophone, naming Hodges and Benny Carter as the two at the top with Willie Smith a rank below.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: When you first went out with him, did you find that exciting to be part of a group that Louis was...?
Louis was nothin' but another trumpet player to me. There was nothin' great about Louis to me. He was just another trumpet player and had some work, that's all. He was no different than nobody else.
But I mean, didn't you find him... You've said other times that there's nobody like him as far as... I mean, he was the greatest...
He could blow his horn, but he didn't excite me. I wasn't interested in trumpet music. He didn't excite me.
I mean, he was good, just like you'd see a whole lot of good piano players. But if you're not interested in piano, it didn't mean nothin'.
Saxophonists was what you were interested in.
Just one saxophonist I was interested in.
That's the only one. Even Benny Carter, great as he was -- and I admire him to the utmost. He's a real artist. He didn't excite me.
Well, what about somebody like Willie Smith?

Oh, he was in my classification. I class him down there with me. There wasn't but two...you know what I mean, two tops, and that was Johnny and Benny -- in my classification. Everybody else, they were down there with me. Yeah, Willie was a great musician. And there was a lot of others. But there was not one, but two at the top, and that was Johnny Hodges and Benny Carter. Johnny was playin' things, he didn't know what he was playin', and Benny was playin' everything, and he did know what he was playin'. Yup, there were some great musicians back in those days...
